zh: 每个骨架独立判断。固定字母不能改，必须与word同位置的字母相同；短横线只能复制该骨架里本来就有的字母，复制不消耗、可以重复使用。
所以一个骨架合法当且仅当：每个固定位置都与word相同，并且每个短横线处word需要的字母都出现在该骨架的字母集合中。全是短横线的骨架没有来源字母，必然失败。
对每个骨架先建出26个字母的出现集合，再逐位检查；通过就把原骨架追加到结果中（保留输入顺序和重复项）。先输出匹配个数，再逐行输出原骨架。
en: Judge each skeleton on its own. Fixed letters cannot change and must equal the letter of word at the same position; a hyphen may only copy a letter the skeleton already contains, and copying consumes nothing, so a letter can be reused.

So a skeleton matches exactly when every fixed position equals word and every letter word needs at a hyphen appears in the skeleton's letter set. A skeleton made only of hyphens has no source letter and always fails.

For each skeleton build its set of present letters, then check position by position; on success append the original skeleton to the result, keeping input order and duplicates. Print the number of matches, then the original skeletons one per line.

explanationEn:
## Pinned original source and corrections

The original SIG OCR008 at the pinned commit e66f809f4c953bce129f68491726176615db6afc defines: only hyphens are replaced, the replacement characters come from the same original skeleton, and other positions cannot change. In the original example, when he-lo becomes hello, the original l is still kept, which shows that characters are copied rather than moved. Every hyphen follows the same replacement rule, and the source specifies no consumption or usage limit, so an extra rule that a letter can be copied only once must not be added. Therefore one existing letter can fill several hyphens; a skeleton whose hyphens have no source letter matches no non-empty word.

The list in 008 mistakenly writes he-o (length 4), but every skeleton is guaranteed to have the same length as hello; 009 clearly writes he--o and explains that both hyphens need l while the skeleton has no l, so it is restored to he--o according to 009, without adding characters by guesswork. The original word=hello, skeletons [he-lo,he--o,-ell-,hello], and original output [he-lo,hello] are kept. The other two public examples are added by this site.

009/010 give the full domain: word consists only of lowercase English letters with length 1..100; there are 1..100 skeletons, each of the same length as word and containing only lowercase letters and hyphens. The result keeps the original order and duplicates, and an empty list is returned when nothing matches. This site's input is word, the number of skeletons, and the skeletons; the output first gives the number of matches and then the original skeletons line by line, with 0 meaning an empty list. This only makes the array serialization explicit and does not change the return value. Upstream code was not executed.

## Proof of correctness

For each skeleton, first build the set of letters it already contains. Check position by position: a fixed letter must equal the corresponding letter of word; the letter a hyphen needs must be in that set. If any check fails, that position cannot legally become the target, so the whole skeleton has no solution. When all checks pass, independently copying each needed letter into the hyphens produces word, so the condition is also sufficient. Appending the original skeletons in input order naturally keeps order and duplicates, and the replaced word is not output.

Let m be the number of skeletons and n the length of word; the time is O(mn), the extra working space is O(26), and storing the return value takes O(mn) characters, which is tiny for the full 100×100 range.

## Independent verification

The small-domain oracle first enumerates every combination of source letters for the hyphens, builds the complete candidate string, and compares it with word, without calling the set-based position check. The 163 unique oracle cases include the original example, repeated copying, all-hyphen skeletons, duplicate skeletons, and conflicts at fixed positions. In addition, all word and skeleton combinations of length 1..4 over a two-letter alphabet are enumerated exhaustively.

The large domain uses another decision method: count the character frequencies demanded by hyphen targets and compare them with the support set of positive frequencies in the original skeleton, while also checking the fixed positions; the number of demands is not limited. The official inputs include several groups of 100 skeletons of length 100, all 26 letters, a single source copied 99 times, empty results, and mixtures of order and duplicates. The two negative controls respectively wrongly limit how many times a source character can be copied and allow replacement with any letter; a kill is counted only after all official inputs exit normally.
